'''Nicolae Popescu''' ({{IPA|ro|nikoˈla.e poˈpesku|lang}}; 22 September 1937 – 29 July 2010) was a [[Romania]]n [[mathematician]] and professor at the [[University of Bucharest]]. He also held a research position at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]], and was elected a [[List of members of the Romanian Academy|corresponding Member]] of the [[Romanian Academy]] in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://acad.ro/bdar/armembriLit.php?vidT=P|title=Membrii Academiei Române din 1866 până în prezent |language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref>

He is best known for his contributions to [[algebra]] and the theory of [[abelian categories]]. From 1964 to 2007 he collaborated with [[Pierre Gabriel]] on the characterization of abelian categories; their best-known result is the [[Gabriel–Popescu theorem]], published in 1964.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Gabriel | first1=Pierre | author1-link=Pierre Gabriel|last2=Popesco | first2=Nicolae | title=Caractérisation des catégories abéliennes avec générateurs et limites inductives exactes | mr=0166241  | year=1964 | journal=[[Comptes rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]] | volume=258 | pages=4188–4190}}</ref>   His areas of expertise were [[category theory]], [[abelian category|abelian categories]] with applications to [[ring (mathematics)|rings]] and [[Module (mathematics)|modules]], [[adjoint functors]], [[Limit (category theory)|limits and colimits]], the theory of sheaves, the theory of [[ring theory|rings]], [[field (mathematics)|fields]] and [[polynomial]]s, and [[Valuation (algebra)|valuation theory]]. He also had interests and published in [[algebraic topology]], [[algebraic geometry]], [[commutative algebra]], [[K-theory]], [[class field theory]], and [[functional analysis|algebraic function theory]].

==Biography==
Popescu was born on September 22, 1937, in [[Strehaia|Strehaia-Comanda]], [[Mehedinți County]], [[Romania]]. In 1954 he graduated from the [[Carol I National College|Carol I High School]] in [[Craiova]] and went on to study mathematics at the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]]. In  his third year of studies he was expelled from the university, having been  deemed "hostile to the regime" for remarking that "the achievements of American scientists are also worth consideration."<ref name="ziua">{{cite news|url=https://www.ziuaveche.ro/exclusiv-zv/intalnirile-zv/nicolae-popescu-povestea-incredibila-a-unui-geniu-al-matematicii-romanesti-49632.html|title=Nicolae Popescu. Povestea incredibilă a unui geniu al matematicii românești|newspaper=Ziua Veche| first=Iolanda |last=Malamen|date=September 3, 2011 |language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Cernea">{{cite web|url=https://www.cafeneauapolitica.ro/geniu-al-matematicii-care-a-copilarit-intr-o-suburbie-a-orasului-strehaia/|title=Geniu al matematicii care a copilărit într-o suburbie a orașului Strehaia| website=www.cafeneauapolitica.ro|first=Valentin|last=Cernea|language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref> He then went back home to Strehaia, where he worked for a year in a collective farm, after which he was admitted in 1959 to the [[University of Bucharest]], only to start anew as a freshman. Popescu  earned his [[Master of Science|M.S.]] degree in mathematics in 1964, and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in mathematics in 1967, with a thesis titled as ''Krull–Remak–Schmidt Theorem and Theory of Decomposition'' written under the direction of {{ill|Gheorghe Galbură|ro}}.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=127579}}</ref> He was awarded a [[D. Phil.]] degree (Doctor Docent) in 1972, also by the University of Bucharest.

While still a student, Popescu focused on [[category theory]]. He first approached the general theory, with its connections to homological algebra and algebraic topology, then shifted his focus to the theory of [[Abelian category|Abelian categories]], being one of the main promoters of this theory in Romania.<ref name="bull"/> He carried out mathematics studies at the Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy in the Algebra research group,<ref name="algebra">{{cite web| url=http://www.imar.ro/organization/people/wgrList.php?ID=4&DEN=Algebra|title=Algebra Research Group|publisher=[[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]]|language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref> and also had international collaborations on three continents. He shared many moral, ethical, and religious values with [[Alexander Grothendieck]], who visited the Faculty of Mathematics in Bucharest in 1968. Like Grothendieck, he had a long-standing interest in category theory and  [[number theory]], and supported promising young mathematicians in his fields of interest. He also promoted the early developments of category theory applications in [[mathematical biology|relational biology]] and mathematical biophysics/[[mathematical biology]].

==Academic positions==
Popescu was appointed as a Lecturer at the University of Bucharest in 1968, where he taught graduate students until 1972. Starting in 1964, he also held a research appointment at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]].<ref name="vita">{{cite web|url=https://www.imar.ro/~nipopesc/|title=Curriculum Vitae – Nicolae Popescu|publisher=[[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]]|language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref><ref name="bull">{{cite journal|last1=Popescu|first1= Elena Liliana|last2= Zaharescu|first2= Alexandru|author2-link=Alexandru Zaharescu|title=A tribute to Professor Nicolae Popescu (1937–2010)|journal= Bull. Math. Soc. Sci. Math. Roumanie |series=Nouvelle Série |volume=56(104)|year=2013|issue =1|pages=3–10|mr=3076686|url=https://ssmr.ro/bulletin/pdf/56-1/survey15ian.pdf}}</ref> The institute was closed in 1976 by order of [[Nicolae Ceaușescu]] (for reasons related to his daughter [[Zoia Ceaușescu]], who had been hired at the institute two years before), but was reopened in 1990, after the [[Romanian Revolution]].

==Publications==
{{Scholia}}
Between 1962 and 2008, Popescu published more than 102 papers in peer-reviewed mathematics journals, several monographs on the theory of sheaves, and several books on [[category theory|abelian category theory]] and [[abstract algebra]], including

* {{Cite book|first=Nicolae|last= Popescu|title=Elemente de teoria algebrică a numerelor|publisher= Universitatea București|date= 1968|trans-title=Elements of the Algebraic Theory of Numbers|language=ro}}
* {{Cite book|first1=Nicolae|last1= Popescu|first2=Alexandru|last2=Radu|title=Teoria categoriilor și a fasciculelor| publisher= Editura Științifică|year= 1971|trans-title=Category Theory and Sheaves|language=ro}}
* {{Cite book|first=Nicolae|last= Popescu|title=Categorii abeliene|publisher= Editura Academiei|year= 1971|trans-title=Abelian Categories|language=ro|mr=0322011}}
* {{Cite book|first=Nicolae|last= Popescu|title=Abelian categories with applications to rings and modules|publisher=Academic Press|series= London Mathematical Society Monographs | volume=3|location=London|year=1973|isbn=0-12-561550-7|mr=0340375}}
* {{Cite book|first1=Nicolae|last1= Popescu| last2=Popescu|first2= Liliana| title=Theory of categories|publisher=Martinus Nijhoff Publishers, The Hague; Sijthoff & Noordhoff International Publishers, Alphen aan den Rijn|year=1979|isbn=90-286-0168-6|mr=0538276|doi=10.1007/978-94-009-9550-5}}

In a [[Alexander Grothendieck|Grothendieck]]-like, energetic style, he initiated and provided scientific leadership to several seminars on category theory, sheaves and abstract algebra, which resulted in a continuous stream of high-quality mathematical publications in international, peer-reviewed mathematics journals by several members participating in his Seminar series.

==Personal life==
Popescu died in Bucharest on July 29, 2010.<ref name="Cernea" /> He is survived by his wife, Professor Dr. {{ill|Elena Liliana Popescu|ro}} (a mathematician, poet, literary translator and editor), and their three children, one of whom, {{ill|Dan Cristian Popescu|ro}}, is a politician.<ref name="ziua" />

==Recognition==
In 1971, Popescu received the [[Simion Stoilow Prize]] in Mathematics of the Romanian Academy. He was elected President of the Romanian Mathematical Society in 1990<ref name="Cernea"/> and a corresponding Member of the Romanian Academy in 1997. On the 80th anniversary of his birthday, the Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics at the University of Bucharest and the Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy organized a conference in his memory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://unibuc.ro/sesiune-comemorativa-dedicata-mentorului-nicolae-popescu-membru-al-academiei-romane-si-creator-al-scolii-romanesti-de-algebra-moderna-si-teoria-numerelor/|title=Sesiune comemorativă dedicată mentorului Nicolae Popescu, membru al Academiei Române și creator al Școlii românești de Algebră modernă și Teoria numerelor|publisher=[[University of Bucharest]]|date=June 29, 2017|language=ro|access-date=May 19, 2020}}</ref>
